Owner rulings (2026-10-07): names **pack** / **Maester Packs**; domain **packs.maester.dev** (maester.dev DNS is on Cloudflare); site + small Worker API (+ D1) on Cloudflare, indexing/scanning in GitHub Actions on a public repo (free minutes), keep costs ~$0–5/month; **binaries allowed** but flagged High risk (risk levels Low/Medium/High/Blocked, like skills.sh audits); **v1 runs packs in-process** (isolation via containers later; keep the hosted-service angle generic in public docs); **no verification programme in v1** — badges instead: Official, Microsoft MVP (from the MVP directory API the `merill/newsletter` repo syncs, `app/src/lib/server/authors/mvp-api.ts`), GitHub-verified org. Publisher-side scanners (Codacy/CodeRabbit) shown only as "repository signals".

Design review of 2026-10-07 fully folded in (fork-commit reachability, single loader gate, packs can't pose as built-ins, namespaced connector services `<CODE>.<Platform>`, -IncludePackScopes/MissingScope, phase-1 blocklist with serial/expiry/offline root key, split scan/publish indexer, **no archive mirror (Merill ruled: never cache repos in Cloudflare; a pack gone from GitHub is skipped — NotRun `PackUnavailable` + report warning)**, lifecycle states, numeric IDs, ID ledger, pack API contract, AllSigned/WDAC, terms/takedowns, /p/ routes, maester365 code `MAES`).

**Why:** Merill wants to review the full design before implementation.

Pack test IDs are `MP.<code>.<number>` (e.g. MP.CNT.0001): `MP.` reserved prefix, 2–5 char code (letters/digits, starts with a letter) held by the **publisher (GitHub user/org, numeric owner ID)**, claimed at the first index of any of its repos, first come first served — no PR; one code per owner, permanent, shared by all its packs (index keeps IDs unique across them); every not-listed version gets an indexing status with reason + fix (doc 7.7, packs.maester.dev/status/{owner}/{repo}, Test-MtPack -Remote); `Find-MtPack -Code` / packs.maester.dev/codes/<CODE> lookup; anti-squat: account >30 days, one claim/day, unlisted claims lapse after 90 days. Also ruled: list on first passing install (owner account >30 days), **one new pack per owner per day**, Astro, High-risk packs shown by default, MVP API best-effort, first official pack Google Workspace.

**Under discussion (2026-10-08, community feedback from TestimoX and LeastPrivilegedMSGraph; NOT yet in the design doc — Merill wants the doc updated only after the Discord discussion ends):** outside tools run as their own step and the pack's connector only reads the output file (no signing; schema-version + max-age checks); **hybrid module-backed packs** (code in the publisher's PowerShell module, pack = manifest + build-generated static catalog + docs, `RequiresModules` + `Provider {Module, ApiVersion}`; chosen over Gallery-hosted packs so GitHub/MVP badges still validate); Maester never installs modules (generated `Install-Module` command; missing → tests skipped); publisher Setup tab; rule catalogs; coverage as own result (`NotCollected`, opt-in CI); own auth libs wrapped as connectors + run-scoped cache; permissions beyond Graph (Entra/Azure RBAC/Exchange roles, `MissingPermission`); connection targets via `Connections.<Service>`/parameter kinds/families. Mode names proposed: code = **Script pack** / **Module pack**; data = **Live** / **Import** / **Collect** (optional Collect hook once per run + Release hook, off by default). Summarised (with two SVG diagrams) in the overview HTML's "Under discussion" section.

**How to apply:** Only owner-side setup is still open (GitHub App, signing key, Cloudflare). Never raise or record the existing `InvokeMaester` PostHog run telemetry in the Packs design — Merill ruled it out of scope (opt-out is already documented). Don't implement until he rules. Keep maester-cloud internals out of public docs, as with [[maester-3-design]].

content.text:
My recommendation: build the ideas board on the Maester Packs stack with GitHub sign-in, keep it separate from the Maester Cloud roadmap store, and connect the two by links and an optional account link. Opening Maester Cloud sign-up to everyone is worth doing, but as its own project, not as the way into this feature.

## What exists today

| | maester.dev | Maester Packs | Maester Cloud roadmap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hosting | Static Astro on Cloudflare Pages | Cloudflare Worker + D1 | Azure Functions and Container Apps, Azure Table Storage |
| Sign-in | None | GitHub, through Better Auth | Entra External ID, email and password only |
| Who can sign up | n/a | Anyone with a GitHub account | Paying customers and invited members only |
| Voting and comments | None | None | Votes, suggestions and comments for customers; operators curate features |
| Status | Live | Live | Dev ring only; `/roadmap` returns 404 in prod |

Three facts shape the design:

- **Cloud sign-up is closed on purpose.** A sign-up extension rejects any email that is not a customer or invitee, and the portal API accepts tokens only from its own app and origin.
- **Cloud has one entitlement rule, not per-feature gating.** Every portal endpoint assumes a signed-in person is a paying customer. There is no free tier.
- **The community is already keyed by GitHub handle.** All 893 tests carry `Author`, the contributor registry marks maintainers and MVPs, and CODEOWNERS names the suite teams.

## Recommended design

**Identity: GitHub, the same accounts as Packs.**
- Reuse the Packs Better Auth setup and its D1 user table, matched on GitHub numeric ID.
- Serve the API from a Worker route on `maester.dev/api/...`, so the static site calls it same-origin with a host-only cookie.
- This needs a second GitHub OAuth App, because an OAuth App has one callback URL. It should request `read:user` only.

**Store: D1 for ideas, GitHub issues for the work.**
- Ideas, votes and comments live in D1.
- When a maintainer accepts an idea, the Worker creates a linked issue in `maester365/maester`. From then on the issue is the record of the work.
- I chose this over plain GitHub Discussions because Discussions cannot show role badges, structured test fields (product, suite, control) or roadmap statuses.

**Idea lifecycle.**
- Kinds: new test, change to an existing test, feature, pack, docs.
- Statuses: New → Under review → Accepted → Claimed → In review → Shipped, plus Declined and Duplicate.
- Claiming assigns the GitHub issue and reserves the MT number. A claim lapses after about 30 days without a pull request.
- An idea about an existing test links to its ID, so the catalog page for that test can list its open ideas.

**Roles are derived, never self-declared.**

| Badge | Source |
|---|---|
| Core maintainer | `maintainer: true` in the contributor registry, or the maester365 team |
| Suite owner | CODEOWNERS teams (`core-tests`, `eidsca`, `cisa`) |
| Test author | The test's `Author` attribute, shown on ideas linked to that test |
| Contributor, MVP, Sponsor | Existing contributor and sponsor data |
| Maester Cloud customer | Optional account link (below) |

There is no per-test "owner" field today, only `Author` and `Contributor`. I would start with `Author` and add an owner override only if authors turn out to be absent.

**Votes: one person, one vote, with a breakdown.**
- I recommend against weighting paid votes. On an open-source board it reads as pay-to-win and contradicts "Maester is free" on the pricing page.
- Instead, show the tally by segment (for example "42 votes, 6 from Cloud customers, 3 from sponsors") and let maintainers sort by segment. You get the signal without the optics.
- Customers keep exclusive influence over the Cloud product roadmap, which the pricing already promises.

**Moderation.** Reuse the Packs rules (account older than 30 days, rate limits, admin log) and the Cloud hide reasons, with post-moderation.

## Integrating with the Maester Cloud roadmap

Do not merge the stores. Cloud's tables are keyed by External ID identities, have strict privacy rules (customer identity never leaves Kermit), and are duplicated across three planes.

- **First:** maester.dev gets a roadmap page for the open-source project, with a Maester Cloud tab built from Cloud's public `GET /api/roadmap` at build time. This needs the Cloud roadmap live in prod.
- **Next:** an operator can link a Cloud suggestion about checks or the engine to a community idea. This fits the untracked work-tracking proposal that makes GitHub issues the system of record.
- **Later:** "Connect GitHub" in the Cloud portal. It is opt-in and reveals only a "Maester Cloud customer" badge, no company name.

## Should anyone be able to sign into Maester Cloud?

Yes, eventually, and it matches your goal of free core building blocks with paid features. But it is a bigger change than the ideas board:

1. Replace the single entitlement rule with a feature-to-plan map.
2. Add a free tier to the customer model.
3. Then relax the sign-up gate and add abuse controls.

Doing step 3 first would give free accounts whatever the portal currently assumes every identity may do. If the ideas board stores linked identities (GitHub required, Cloud optional), it will not need rework when this lands.

## Phases

1. Board on maester.dev: sign-in, ideas, votes, comments, badges, promote to issue.
2. Claims, MT reservation, ideas on catalog pages, the open-source roadmap page.
3. Cloud tab and account linking.
4. Cloud free tier and open sign-up (separate project in the cloud repo).

## Decisions for you

- **Vote weighting:** segments instead of weights, as above, or real weights.
- **Where the backend code lives:** the Packs Worker repo is private (`jozrahq`). Reusing it is fastest; a public repo is better for community trust in the voting.
- **Test owner:** `Author` to start, or a new `Owner` attribute now.

# Design: Community ideas and roadmap

> **Status: DRAFT for owner review. Nothing is implemented.** Drafted 2026-11-09.
> Section 11 lists the decisions that are still open. This document covers the
> open-source project only. Maester Cloud has its own product roadmap for its
> customers; section 9 says how the two connect, and nothing here changes how Maester
> Cloud works.

## 1. Summary

Anyone in the community can propose a test, a feature, a pack or a documentation
change on maester.dev, vote and comment on other people's ideas, and take an accepted
idea and implement it. Maintainers triage ideas into a public roadmap. A person's
standing in the project (core maintainer, suite owner, author of the test under
discussion, contributor, sponsor) is shown beside what they write.

The design in one page:

- **Sign in with GitHub**, the same way Maester Packs does. The project already knows
  its community by GitHub handle: every built-in test names its `Author`, the
  contributor registry marks maintainers and MVPs, and CODEOWNERS names the suite
  teams. Section 3.
- **Ideas, votes and comments live in a small database; the work lives in GitHub.**
  When a maintainer accepts an idea, an issue is created in `maester365/maester` and
  linked to it. From then on the issue is the record of the work, and the idea follows
  its state. Section 4.
- **An accepted idea can be claimed.** Claiming assigns the issue and, for a new test,
  reserves its MT number. A claim with no pull request lapses. Section 6.
- **Badges are derived from project data, never self-declared.** Section 7.
- **One person, one vote.** The tally is shown with a breakdown by group, so
  maintainers can see what sponsors or customers want without any vote counting for
  more than another. Section 8.
- **The roadmap is a view of the same data**: accepted, in-progress and shipped ideas,
  grouped by release. Section 5.

## 2. What exists today

| | maester.dev | Maester Packs |
|---|---|---|
| Hosting | Static Astro site on Cloudflare Pages; no server code | Cloudflare Worker with a D1 database; static Astro site served as its assets |
| Sign-in | None | GitHub, through Better Auth |
| Voting, comments | None | None |
| Roles | n/a | Site admins only |

Asking for a test or feature today means a GitHub issue (`1-feature-request.yml`,
labelled `enhancement` and `status: needs triage`) or a discussion. There is no issue
template for a new test, no way to vote beyond reactions, and no page that shows what
is planned. New MT numbers are reserved by commenting on issue 697.

Project data the feature can build on:

- `test-catalog.json`: every test with its `Author`, `Contributor`, product, suite and
  control mappings.
- `contributors.json`: profiles with `maintainer`, `mvp`, tests authored and
  contributed.
- `sponsors.json`: GitHub Sponsors.
- `.github/CODEOWNERS`: the teams that own `tests/maester/`, `tests/eidsca/`,
  `tests/cisa/` and `website/`.
- `.github/labels.json`: `new test`, `enhancement`, `help wanted`, `good first issue`,
  and the `status:`, `product:` and `suite:` families.

## 3. Identity

GitHub is the only sign-in. Reasons:

- People who propose and implement tests have a GitHub account already, and
  implementing an idea ends in a pull request from that account.
- Every badge in section 7 is keyed by GitHub handle or numeric ID.
- Maester Packs already runs this sign-in, so there is one pattern to maintain.

How it is built:

- The API is a Cloudflare Worker on a route of the site's own host
  (`maester.dev/api/community/*`). The static pages call it same-origin, so there is
  no CORS and the session cookie is host-only.
- Better Auth with a GitHub OAuth App, as on Maester Packs. An OAuth App has one
  callback URL, so this is a second app. It requests `read:user` only; team
  membership is read server-side with the project's bot token, not the user's.
- Accounts are matched on the GitHub numeric ID, so a renamed account keeps its
  history. Whether the user table is shared with Maester Packs depends on the decision
  in section 11.2.
- Reading is open to everyone without signing in. Signing in is needed to propose,
  vote, comment or claim.

The user record allows more than one linked identity (GitHub required, others
optional), so a later link to a Maester Cloud account (section 9) needs no rework.

## 4. Data model

D1 tables, beside the Better Auth tables:

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| `ideas` | `id`, `kind`, `title`, `body`, `status`, `author_id`, taxonomy fields (`product`, `suite`, `control`), `test_id` for an idea about an existing test, `issue_number`, `pull_number`, `release`, `duplicate_of`, `hidden`, kept tallies, timestamps |
| `idea_votes` | one row per idea and user |
| `idea_comments` | `idea_id`, `author_id`, `body`, `kind` (`comment` or `event`), `hidden`, `hidden_reason`, `edited`, timestamps |
| `idea_claims` | `idea_id`, `user_id`, `claimed_at`, `expires_at`, `released_at`, `reserved_test_id` |
| `admin_log` | who did what, as on Maester Packs |

Kinds: `test` (a new check), `test-change` (a change to an existing check), `feature`,
`pack`, `docs`.

Taxonomy fields use the keys in `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1` and the
framework files, so an idea for "CIS 5.1.5.1" can be found from that requirement and
checked for duplicates against the catalog before it is accepted.

Role data (section 7) is not stored per user. It is read from the site's generated
JSON and cached, so it changes when the repository changes.

## 5. Lifecycle and roadmap

| Status | Meaning | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| New | Just proposed; visible at once | Author |
| Under review | A maintainer is looking at it | Maintainer |
| Accepted | Wanted; open for someone to take. A GitHub issue exists. | Maintainer |
| Claimed | Someone is implementing it | Claimer |
| In review | A pull request is linked | GitHub webhook |
| Shipped | Merged, with the release it shipped in | GitHub webhook |
| Declined | Not planned, with a reason | Maintainer |
| Duplicate | Merged into another idea; its votes move there | Maintainer |

Accepting an idea creates the issue with the labels the triage rubric gives it
(`new test` or `enhancement`, `product:`, `suite:`, `help wanted`). A webhook from the
repository moves the idea to In review when a pull request references the issue and to
Shipped when it merges. An existing issue can also be attached to an idea, so the
backlog does not have to be re-entered.

The roadmap page shows Accepted, Claimed, In review and Shipped ideas, grouped as
Planned, In progress and Shipped by release. It is built from the same tables; there
is no second list to maintain.

Each test's page in the catalog lists the open ideas linked to it.

## 6. Claiming an idea

- Only Accepted ideas can be claimed, one claimer at a time.
- Claiming assigns the GitHub issue to the claimer. For a `test` idea it also reserves
  the next MT number, replacing the manual comment on issue 697.
- A claim lapses after 30 days with no linked pull request. The claimer gets a
  reminder a week before, and can extend once.
- A maintainer can release any claim.

## 7. Roles and badges

Badges are derived, and shown beside the person's name on ideas and comments.

| Badge | Source |
|---|---|
| Core maintainer | `maintainer: true` in the contributor registry |
| Suite owner | Membership of a CODEOWNERS team, shown on ideas in that suite |
| Test author | The `Author` of the test an idea is linked to, shown on that idea only |
| Contributor | Has a merged contribution |
| Microsoft MVP | The contributor registry |
| Sponsor | GitHub Sponsors |

Maintainers can accept, decline, merge, hide and release claims. Suite owners can do
the same within their suite. Everyone else can propose, vote, comment and claim.

A comment from a maintainer, a suite owner or the test's author is marked as such and
can be pinned above the thread, so the people responsible for a test are easy to find
in a long discussion.

There is no per-test owner field today, only `Author` and `Contributor`. Version 1
uses `Author`. See section 11.3.

## 8. Voting

One vote per person per idea. The author votes for their own idea automatically.
Shipped and declined ideas take no more votes.

The tally shows the total and a breakdown: maintainers, contributors, sponsors and
others. Maintainers can sort by any group.

No group's vote counts for more than another's. A weighted vote on an open-source
board would mean influence can be bought, which is not what "Maester is free" says.
The breakdown gives maintainers the same signal.

## 9. Maester Cloud

Maester Cloud has a product roadmap of its own, for its customers. The two stay
separate: different products, different sign-ins, different audiences.

They connect in three ways, in this order:

1. **Links.** The maester.dev roadmap page links to the Maester Cloud roadmap, and the
   other way round.
2. **Shared ideas.** A customer suggestion that is really about a check or the engine
   can be linked to a community idea, so it is tracked once, in the open.
3. **Account link.** A Maester Cloud customer can choose to connect their GitHub
   account. Their votes are then counted in a "Maester Cloud customers" group in the
   breakdown, and they get a badge. It is opt-in and shows nothing about the customer
   but the badge.

## 10. Moderation and abuse

- A GitHub account must be at least 30 days old to propose, comment or claim, the
  rule Maester Packs uses for publishers.
- Rate limits per account on proposing, commenting and voting.
- Ideas and comments are visible at once and moderated afterwards. A hidden item
  records a reason: spam, off-topic, abusive, personal information, duplicate.
- Every moderation action is written to `admin_log`.
- The site's terms and code of conduct apply; the page links to both.

## 11. Open decisions

1. **Vote weighting.** This draft uses one person, one vote with a breakdown
   (section 8). The alternative is a real weight for some groups.
2. **Where the backend code lives.** Reusing the Maester Packs Worker and database is
   the least work and gives one account across both sites. A public repository of its
   own lets the community read the code that counts their votes.
3. **Test owner.** Version 1 treats a test's `Author` as its owner. If authors turn
   out to be absent, an owner override is needed: a new attribute, or a list kept
   beside the contributor registry.
4. **GitHub Discussions.** Existing idea discussions could be imported as ideas, or
   left where they are with a pointer to the new page.

## 12. Phases

1. **Board.** Sign-in, propose, vote, comment, badges, maintainer triage, accept to a
   GitHub issue.
2. **Implementing.** Claims, MT reservation, webhook status, ideas on catalog pages,
   the roadmap page.
3. **Maester Cloud.** Links, shared ideas, account link.

## 13. Not yet verified

- That a Worker route on `maester.dev/api/*` can sit in front of the Cloudflare Pages
  project as it is deployed today.
- That Better Auth can share a user table between two OAuth Apps on two hosts, if
  decision 11.2 goes that way.
- The cost at community scale; expected to stay inside the same few dollars a month as
  Maester Packs.

11:- The root [.dockerignore](.dockerignore) names `website`/`kermit` and is masked at publish by [publish/overlay/.dockerignore](publish/overlay/.dockerignore). If you change customer-relevant lines in the root file, mirror them in the overlay copy.
12-
13-## Toolchain isolation (do not "unify")
14-
15:Root `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and `Directory.Packages.props` ship to customers, so `website/` and `kermit/` stay out of the root pnpm workspace, the root solution, and root CPM:
16-
17-- `website/Directory.Build.props` and `website/Directory.Packages.props` are inheritance barriers (the website codebase isn't built against the root's TreatWarningsAsErrors/CPM). Keep them.
18-- `kermit/Directory.Packages.props` pins kermit's packages (CPM nearest-wins); kermit otherwise inherits the root Build.props and global.json.
19-- `website/src` is npm (package-lock.json); `website/portal` is pnpm with its own workspace file. Those nested `pnpm-workspace.yaml` files stop pnpm's upward walk — keep them.
20-- `website/portal` consumes the shared design system through a one-way `"@maester-cloud/ui": "file:../../src/ui"` dependency — no root-plane file references `website/`. Its Docker image builds from the **repo-root** context with the allowlist in [website/portal-api/Dockerfile.dockerignore](website/portal-api/Dockerfile.dockerignore). After changing `src/ui` (its `package.json` especially), re-run `pnpm install` in `website/portal` so its lockfile and installed copy stay in sync — the image build's `--frozen-lockfile` fails otherwise.
21-
22-## CI/CD
23-
--
25:- Any push to main touching product paths (see the filter in [auto-release.yml](.github/workflows/auto-release.yml)) cuts a full dev release automatically. Docs, workflows, `publish/`, `website/`, and `kermit/` are outside the filter.
26:- Browser E2E: [tests/e2e](tests/e2e/README.md) (Playwright, against the app image + Azurite) gates every release before `promote-ppe`. A user-facing portal feature or fix ships with a spec there; it is a standalone pnpm package, deliberately outside the root workspace and the publish manifest.
27-- **Deploying a feature: use its runbook.** When asked how to deploy something, or for the next deploy steps, find its runbook under `website/deploy/runbooks/` (feature rollouts are indexed in that folder's README, e.g. `0006-onboarding-emails`) or `kermit/deploy/runbooks/`. Read its **Rollout status** table, then give the steps for the requested ring in runbook order, copying the runbook's commands (one command per `bash` block) rather than composing new ones. The founder runs every elevation, workflow dispatch and Azure write; you only run read-only checks. After a ring's step is done, update the status table in a PR. Before giving the steps for any website or Kermit ring deploy, read the Rollout status table of every feature runbook and include the steps still to do in that ring, in runbook order: infrastructure a new image needs comes before the image, and seed data such as `0008-public-roadmap` is part of the deploy.
28:- Website deploy config source of truth: `website/deploy/environments/{dev,ppe,prod}.json` (domains, resources, GitHub env names, FIC names). Kermit's is `kermit/deploy/environments/{dev,ppe,prod}.json` (own resource group per ring in the ring subscription; see [kermit/deploy/README.md](kermit/deploy/README.md)). The release pipeline itself: [docs/owner-setup-runbook.md](docs/owner-setup-runbook.md) §10.
29-
30-## Portal data scaling
31-
32:Portal pages must stay fast as tenants and runs grow. Before adding or changing a portal page, an `/api` read endpoint, or a background job that reads runs or results, read [docs/portal-read-model-design.md](docs/portal-read-model-design.md) and keep to its scaling rules:
33-
34-- A page load makes a fixed number of API requests; no loader loops over runs or tenants.
35-- Lists and summaries carry no result text; fetch it for one test on demand.
36-- Anything derived only from processed runs is computed when the run is processed, not per request.
37-- Policy, accepted risks and views are applied on read, never stored into a summary.
38-- No request path scans a table partition that grows with history; history is the trailing 120 days per tenant.
39-- Stored summaries hold facts, never a page's layout. A feature that needs a new stored fact says how past runs get it: forward only, backfill from rows, or backfill from reports.
40-- No new always-on Azure service.
